label: L15 · Fungi as Pathogens
rows: True (primary) pathogen
Invades and grows in a HEALTHY host. Can cause systemic, subcutaneous, cutaneous and superficial mycoses. The four true pathogens are thermally dimorphic.
Opportunist

Little or no virulence of its own; needs IMPAIRED defenses (human immunodeficiency virus infection, cancer, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, autoimmune disorder, nosocomial). Once 'harmless' skin or air contaminants.
Thermal dimorphism
MOLD (multicellular) at 30 °C in soil → YEAST (unicellular) at 37 °C in the body. The true pathogen's key adaptation.
Mostly harmless
Relatively nonpathogenic: ~300 of ~100,000 species cause disease. But fungi are the most common PLANT pathogens (potato blights, famines).
Emerging
Mycoses ~10% of nosocomial infections and rising; dermatophytes may be becoming true pathogens; invasive fungal disease rising in the immunocompromised.
Host defense
Skin, mucous membranes, cilia; MOST IMPORTANT = cell-mediated immunity (T cells, cytokines), phagocytosis, inflammation. Reinfection highly likely with opportunists.
Communicable?
Most fungal infections are NOT (no host needed for the life cycle). Exceptions: dermatophytes and Candida (person to person, fomites).
Most prevalent
Dermatophytoses: the most common fungal diseases; often undiagnosed or misdiagnosed as allergy or autoimmune disease.

label: L15 · Diagnosis & Control
rows: Diagnosis
Microscopy of stained specimens + culture on selective and enriched media + biochemical or serological tests.
Sabouraud dextrose agar
Commonly used; its LOW pH inhibits most bacteria but not fungi (chemicals added to block bacteria).
Potassium hydroxide
Lyses human epithelial cells, leaves fungi intact: fungi have a THICKER cell wall.
Flowchart clues

Wood's light on hairs · negative stain for a capsule · GERM TUBE test (yeasts in serum 2–4 h sprout hyphal tubes) · culture at 25–30 °C AND 37 °C to demonstrate dimorphism · long incubations (up to 8 weeks; 4 weeks for hair, skin, nails) · animal inoculation only when other methods fail.
Stains (slide 18)
Aspergillus = BRANCHED SEPTATE hyphae in sputum; germinating Candida albicans = young hypha from a yeast.
No vaccines
Immunization typically ineffective because REINFECTION is exceedingly common.
Control
Drugs: amphotericin B, flucytosine, azoles, nystatin · surgical removal of damaged tissue · prevention = respirator masks, protective clothing, hygiene.
Amphotericin B

Drug of choice for many infections; from Streptomyces (a soil bacterium); complexes with fungal membrane LIPIDS → leakage; TOXIC because fungi and humans are both eukaryotes (fatigue, weakness, fever, arrhythmia): 'ampho-terrible'.

label: L15 · The True Pathogens (Systemic)
rows: Shared pattern
Endemic regions; soil or animal waste with conidia is DISTURBED → spores INHALED → yeasts in the lungs → may go systemic; can also inoculate broken skin.
Histoplasma capsulatum

OHIO VALLEY FEVER; the MOST COMMON true pathogen; eastern/central United States, Latin America, Africa; moist nitrogen-rich soil with BIRD AND BAT GUANO; inhaled microconidia; NOT person to person; yeast multiplies inside phagocytes; most recover.
Coccidioides immitis

VALLEY FEVER; southwestern United States to Mexico, Central/South America; alkaline, salty soil of semiarid, hot climates; dust (farming, construction, digs, dust storms); drought-rain-wind cycles; ARTHROCONIDIA → SPHERULES with endospores; risk: African descent, age 40–60+, dust exposure; most need no treatment.
Blastomyces dermatitidis

NORTH AMERICAN blastomycosis; forest soil, decaying wood, manure; Midwest/Southeast and southern Canada; inhaled conidia → yeasts; MIMICS LUNG CANCER on chest X-ray; dogs, cats, horses; chronic skin nodules, later bone and nervous system.
Paracoccidioides brasiliensis
Central/South America (Brazil); the RAREST primary mycosis; inhalation (lung) or inoculation (skin); rural farm workers, poor nutrition, male, over 40; usually mild, self-limiting.

label: L15 · Subcutaneous, Cutaneous, Superficial
rows: Subcutaneous mycoses
Fungus pushed into TRAUMATIZED skin; inhibited by the warmth of blood and viscera, so rarely disseminate; progressive tissue destruction.
Sporothrix schenckii

ROSE-GARDENER'S disease: thorn, wood, bare roots; saprobe in soil; garden centers, nurseries, pine straw, hay; LYMPHOCUTANEOUS = nodule then spread to nearby lymph nodes; heat packs, super-saturated potassium iodide; systemic: amphotericin B and/or itraconazole.
Dermatophytes

Keratin ONLY (skin, hair, scalp, nails) = ringworm/tinea; Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton (39 species); agent varies case to case; reservoirs humans, animals, soil; hardy spores + abraded skin + close contact or fomites; long infection, then inflammation and allergy to fungal proteins.
★ Latin names
The deck: 'Focus on the Latin names for each body part/region' → capitis, barbae, corporis, cruris, pedis, manuum, unguium (table above).
Tinea treatment
Topical AZOLES for several weeks ± oral antifungals; debridement; ultraviolet light.
Superficial mycoses

Tinea VERSICOLOR = Malassezia furfur, a YEAST (scaling, mottling). WHITE piedra = Trichosporon (pubic/axillary hair). BLACK piedra = Piedraia (scalp hairs). Piedras non-contagious, hygiene; rare in the United States.

label: L15 · The Opportunists
rows: Candida albicans

The DOMINANT opportunist; normal flora (mouth, genitalia, large intestine, skin); ~70% of nosocomial fungal infections; usually endogenous, but spread by surgery, childbirth, breast-feeding, sex; off-white pasty colony smelling of BAKING BREAD.
Candida forms

THRUSH (thick white adherent growth) · vulvovaginal (to unprotected partners, esp. uncircumcised males) · cutaneous in moist skin and burns · intertriginous (obesity). Diagnosis: budding yeast + PSEUDOHYPHAE; species by selective differential media.
Candida auris
Emerging invasive candidiasis; HOSPITAL OUTBREAKS hard to eradicate (drug resistant, thermoresistant, partly disinfectant resistant); first found in an EAR infection, Japan 2009.
Cryptococcus neoformans

#1 CRITICAL on the World Health Organization list; ENCAPSULATED yeast in soil around urban PIGEON roosts; healthy people resist; lungs → MENINGES and brain; NEGATIVE STAIN; serology and biochemistry best; amphotericin B + fluconazole.
Pneumocystis jirovecii

Unicellular fungus; the MOST PROMINENT opportunistic infection in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome; also kidney transplant; widespread silent exposure (antibody titers); secretions block breathing; PENTAMIDINE + CO-TRIMOXAZOLE (not antifungals); a fungus by genetics.
Aspergillus fumigatus

Airborne soil mold; azole resistance from CROP SPRAYING; #3 critical; lungs → FUNGAL BALLS; sinuses, ear canals, eyelids, conjunctiva; invasive necrotic pneumonia, brain, heart; leukemia, transplant, cystic fibrosis.
Mucormycosis

Zygomycota (Rhizopus, Mucor) saprobes; 'black mould' in India (steroids, uncontrolled DIABETES); nose, eyes, heart, brain in diabetes, leukemia, malnutrition; kwashiorkor gut form; cut out tissue + amphotericin B.
Fusarium · eumycetoma
Fusarium: tropical soil mold; contaminated CONTACT LENSES, toenails, burns. Eumycetoma: poor countries; male, 11–30, farmer, no shoes; long-term drugs, amputation.

label: L15 · Allergies, Toxins & How We Get Them
rows: Allergies
Spores → atopic allergy, seasonal allergy, asthma; farmer's lung, teapicker's lung, bark stripper's disease.
Mycotoxicoses

Ingested or inhaled fungal toxins: AFLATOXIN (liver, cancer co-factor; grains, corn, peanuts; kills turkeys) · ERGOT (rye, Claviceps, lysergic acid; Salem) · STACHYBOTRYS (sick building, 'black mold'; not mucormycosis).
Objective 2: inhaled
Systemic true pathogens (disturbed soil, guano, dust); Cryptococcus (pigeon roost soil); Aspergillus and Zygomycota (air).
Objective 2: inoculated
Sporothrix (thorns, wood); Paracoccidioides skin form; nail extensions (tinea unguium).
Objective 2: contact
Dermatophytes (people, animals, fomites, public surfaces; barbae mainly from animals) · Candida (surgery, birth, breast-feeding, sex; usually endogenous).
Not communicable
Most fungi; Histoplasma explicitly NOT person to person; piedras non-contagious.
